To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

crosslinked copoly(2-nonyloxy-2-oxazine)s can be synthesized from renewable resources, and these materials show electrical properties in the same range of polyamides, making these copoly(oxazoline)s a promising alternative to polyamides for electronic applications.
(co)polymer networks based on renewable resources are suitable for use as insulators in electrical applications.

(co)polyoxazolines derived from renewable resources can be crosslinked to form polymer networks with permittivity and loss factor in the same range of values as polyamides, but with a lower environmental burden.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of (co)polymer materials from renewable resources and with the development of these materials for electronic applications, such as dielectrics and insulators.
the synthesis of poly(2-oxa-zoline)s and their crosslinked derivatives from renewable resources and their application as insulators in electronics.
the development of “green” polymers for the application as insulators in the field of electronics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
crosslinked (co)-poly(2- oxazoline)s can act as insulators for electronic applications.

the copolymerization of fatty acid derived monomers and the crosslinking of the obtained copolymers by UV-induced thiol–ene reactions are promising routes for “green” materials for electronic applications.
the copolymer networks of poly(2-nonyloxazoline)80 and poly(2-oxa-2-decenyl)20 are “green” alternatives to polyamide networks as insulators for electronic applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cationic polymerization of renewable monomers and the subsequent crosslinking using UV-induced thiol–ene reactions are suitable strategies for the preparation of “green” polymeric materials with a high degree of functionalization and with properties suitable for electronic applications.

the cationic ROP of monomers that are derived from fatty acids can be applied for the preparation of crosslinked copoly(2-nonyloxazoline) networks that can be used as medium insulators in electronic devices.
crosslinked poly(2-oxa-zoline)s from renewable resources can be used as insulators for electronic applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
(co)polymer networks derived from renewable resources can be designed as “green” materials for electronic applications.
the permittivity as a function of frequency and temperature can be tuned by varying the network density.
the complex permittivities of the crosslinked copoly(2oxazoline)s increase with increasing temperature and decreasing density of the network.
